title.en: Why does the sugar mill stand in the cane field?

text.en: No one builds a sugar mill in a big city; they stand next to sugarcane fields. Cane loses weight and sugar as it dries, and it is bulky to carry. Where an industry stands is never an accident; it follows its raw material. This lesson takes the book's industries one by one and asks that same question each time.

An industry converts raw materials into finished goods, which is why this sector is called the value addition sector, and by raw material industries are agro-based, forest-based or mineral-based.
Cotton textiles is the broad term covering cotton, jute, wool, silk and synthetic fibre; India's textile sector is the second largest in the world and the third largest producer of cotton.
The first cotton mill was set up at Fort Gloster near Kolkata in 1818, and the cotton textile industry is today the largest organised modern industry of India.
Mumbai is called the Manchester of India because black cotton soil, a humid climate, the port, hydropower, a good market and transport all help the mills there.
Coimbatore, with about 200 of Tamil Nadu's 435 mills, is the Manchester of South India, and Erode, Tiruppur, Karur, Madurai, Salem and Virudhunagar are other centres.
Jute is the golden fibre, a natural, renewable, biodegradable material; the first jute mill started at Rishra near Kolkata in 1854, and mills crowd the Hooghly river belt in West Bengal.
India is the top producer of raw jute and makes gunny bags, canvas, hessian, twine and carpets from it.
India is the second largest producer of raw silk after China, Karnataka is the largest silk producing state, and the Central Silk Technological Research Institute at Bengaluru was set up in 1983.
Sugar is made from sugarcane, India is the second largest producer after Brazil, and mills are located near the cane fields because cane is bulky and loses weight; Uttar Pradesh is the leading producer, followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Paper is the main forest-based industry using wood pulp, bamboo, salai and sabai grass, waste paper and bagasse; the first mill was at Serampore in 1812, and West Bengal is the largest producer.
Iron and steel is called a basic metallurgical industry because machines, locomotives, automobiles and railways use it as raw material, so a country's steel capacity shows its industrial development.
The first attempt to make iron and steel was at Porto Novo in Tamil Nadu in 1830, and modern industry began with Tata Iron and Steel Company at Sakchi, now Jamshedpur, in 1907.
Steel is concentrated in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha because of the nearness of Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro and Karanpura coalfields and the iron ore of Mayurbhanj and Keonjhar, with limestone, dolomite and manganese close by.
Public sector steel plants include Bhilai with Russia in 1957, Durgapur with Britain in 1959, Rourkela with Germany in 1965, Bokaro with Russia in 1972, and Salem Steel in Tamil Nadu in 1982 for stainless steel.
India's first automobile company was Premier Automobiles at Kurla in Mumbai in 1947, Chennai is the Detroit of Asia, and India is the seventh largest producer of automobiles.
Heavy electrical goods come from BHEL with plants at Haridwar, Bhopal, Hyderabad, Jhansi, Bengaluru and Tiruchirappalli, and Bengaluru is the Electronic Capital of India.
The software industry began in 1970 with Tata Consultancy Services, now has over 500 companies exporting to about 95 countries, and the Make in India programme of 2014 supports manufacturing.
Indian industries face power shortage, lack of large land blocks, poor access to credit, high interest rates, scarce cheap labour, lack of technical training and poor living conditions near industrial estates.

problem.en: Why is a sugar mill built near sugarcane fields while an electronics factory can stand in a city like Bengaluru?

text.en: Sugarcane is bulky and loses weight and sugar as time passes after harvest.
So transport cost and loss are lowest if the mill is next to the fields.

why.en: Raw material that is heavy and perishable pulls the industry toward it.

text.en: Electronic parts are small, light and durable, so they can be brought from anywhere, and the factory can stand where skilled people and markets are.

why.en: Location follows the nature of the raw material.

prompt.en: Explain how raw material decides where an industry stands, using steel in Jamshedpur and cotton mills in Mumbai.

requiredIdeas.en: Steel needs coal and iron ore, found in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal
Cotton mills at Mumbai got black cotton soil, port, humid climate and market
Heavy or perishable raw materials pull the industry toward them

commonMisconceptions.en: The first cotton mill was at Mumbai (it was at Fort Gloster near Kolkata)
Sugar mills are built far from cane fields (they stand near them)

points.en: Industries are agro-based, forest-based or mineral-based according to the raw material.
Cotton: Mumbai is the Manchester of India, Coimbatore the Manchester of South India; jute is the golden fibre.
Iron and steel started at Jamshedpur in 1907 and clusters near coal and iron ore.
Chennai is the Detroit of Asia, Bengaluru the Electronic Capital; challenges include power, land, credit and training.
